The standard score SS uses the classic Wechsler scale (mean 100, SD 15); 85–115 is the average normative range. The percentile PR is derived from the standard normal CDF Φ, computing the error function via the Abramowitz–Stegun rational approximation (precision ≈ 1.5×10⁻⁷). A dimension score is the arithmetic mean of its subtests' standard scores; the composite is the mean of all subtests. Reaction-time indicators are first trimmed: when trials ≥ 5, the slowest trial is dropped before averaging to reduce single lapse bias.

Device differences directly affect reaction-time indicators: touchscreens and Bluetooth keyboards are typically 20–60 ms slower than wired keyboards, so cross-device comparison is of limited value; use the same device for longitudinal tracking.

综合性认知能力评估工具，用 8 项经典分测验覆盖注意力、工作记忆、加工速度与执行: A comprehensive cognitive battery covering four dimensions — attention, working memory, processing speed and executive function — with 8 classic subtests: simple reaction time, choice reaction time, digit span forward/backward, Symbol Digit Modalities, Stroop interference, 2-back working memory, and TMT-A/B. Each subtest gives instructions and a practice trial before scoring; raw scores are converted via four age-band norms into standard scores (mean 100, SD 15) and percentiles, then rendered as a 4-axis radar, itemized table and strength/weakness interpretation. History is stored locally and exportable to CSV and PNG.
